claims.quote: The demonstration that no possible combination of known substances, known forms of machinery, and known forms of force can be united in a practicable machine by which men shall fly long distances through the air, seems to the writer as complete as it is possible for the demonstration of any physical fact to be.
claims.description: Heavier-than-air flying machines using known materials and power cannot carry people long distances.

claims.quote: May not our mechanicians, in like manner, be ultimately forced to admit that aerial flight is one of that great class of problems with which man can never cope
claims.description: Human flight may turn out to be an impossible problem like squaring the circle.

claims.quote: then may gravitation be overcome and then may men build, not merely airships, but ships which shall fly above the air, and transport their passengers from continent to continent with the speed of the celestial motions.
claims.description: Understanding and controlling gravity would allow spaceships carrying passengers between continents at celestial speeds.

claims.quote: it is not impossible that the twentieth century may be destined to make known natural forces which will enable us to fly from continent to continent with a speed far exceeding that of the bird.
claims.description: New natural forces discovered in the twentieth century may enable ultra-fast intercontinental flight.

claims.quote: but let us discover a substance a hundred times as strong as steel, and with that some form of force hitherto unsuspected which will enable us to utilize this strength
claims.description: A material a hundred times stronger than steel plus an unknown force might make a flying machine possible.

claims.quote: or let us discover some way of reversing the law of gravitation so that matter may be repelled by the earth instead of attracted—then we may have a flying-machine.
claims.description: Anti-gravity that repels matter from the earth would allow a flying machine.

claims.quote: he might find the result to be, ideally at least, a ship which would be driven through the air by a steam-engine with a velocity far exceeding that of the fleetest Atlantic liner.
claims.description: A huge steel dirigible airship, designed by naval engineers, could cross the air faster than an Atlantic liner.

claims.quote: Even if a dirigible balloon should cross the Atlantic, it does not follow that it could compete with the steamship in carrying passengers and freight.
claims.description: Airships would not be commercially competitive with steamships.

claims.quote: It may certainly seem singular if man is never to discover any combination of substances which, under the influence of some such agency as an electric current, shall expand and contract like a muscle.
claims.description: Artificial muscle materials that contract under electric current may someday be discovered, though not soon.

claims.quote: the smallest possible flying-machine will be the first one to be successful.
claims.description: Successful flying machines will first be tiny, and size scaling limits larger ones.

claims.quote: Yes, a sufficient number of humming-birds, if we could combine their forces, would carry an aerial excursion party of human beings through the air.
claims.description: A swarm of thousands of tiny flying machines combined could carry a person.

claims.quote: A nearly horizontal surface, swinging around in a circle, on a vertical axis, like the wings of a windmill moving horizontally, will fulfil all the conditions.
claims.description: A rotating-wing lift system with counter-rotating sails (helicopter-like) could provide sustained lift.
